    Lemma 11.1: two associative tables #

    binary-families.tex (lem:two-associative-tables): "Let S be a finite set with an absorbing zero, and let m, m_* be associative products on S […] Suppose m_*(a,b) = m(a,b) whenever m(a,b) ≠ 0. Put Z = {(a,b) : m(a,b) = 0, m_*(a,b) ≠ 0} and let ε_z be the bilinear map supported at z = (a,b) with value m_*(a,b) […] Assume all nested insertions vanish. There is an equivalence relation on Z such that, over every commutative ring R, the Hochschild two-cocycles among the cochains ∑ a_z ε_z have basis μ_E = ∑_{z∈E} ε_z, indexed by its classes. The product m + ∑_E T_E μ_E is associative over the polynomial ring in the T_E. When every T_E is zero or one, S ∖ {0} is a multiplicative basis for this product."

    Formalization: an R-algebra Λ with a basis b indexed by S (the nonzero elements), b x * b y = b (m x y) or 0 (m : S → S → Option S), and a second associative table ms agreeing with m where m is nonzero. For coefficients a : S → S → R, eps a is ∑_{z ∈ Z} a_z ε_z. Each cocycle equation at a basis triple t has the form (a (L t) − a (Rt t)) • U t = 0 with a common value U t (dEps_eq). Hence a cochain is a cocycle iff a is constant along the relation Rel of the nonvanishing equations (isCocycle_iff); the product m + eps T is associative for such T (assoc_add_eps), and has b as a multiplicative basis when T takes values 0, 1 (mul_basis_of_binary).

                    Lemma 11.1, binary points: when T takes the values 0 and 1, the basis is multiplicative for m + ∑ T_z ε_z.
